In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: smbdirect: don't wait for RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED in smbdirect_socket_destroy_sync() smbdirect_socket_destroy_sync() waited for RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED after smbdirect_socket_cleanup_work() called rdma_disconnect(). That can take very long, e.g. if the peer just disappeared, until the rdma cm gives up, or forever if the event already happened, but the status was overwritten afterwards. This is not needed: smbdirect_socket_destroy() drains the qp under rdma_lock_handler(), destroys it and calls rdma_destroy_id(), which only waits for a currently running event handler and makes sure no further events are delivered. The rest of the disconnect protocol (DREQ/DREP and timewait for IB, abrupt close for iWarp) is handled by the rdma core asynchronously. drivers/nvme/host/rdma.c also just calls rdma_disconnect() and ib_drain_qp() before rdma_destroy_id(). So smbdirect_socket_destroy() now also accepts SMBDIRECT_SOCKET_DISCONNECTING and changes the status to SMBDIRECT_SOCKET_DISCONNECTED itself under rdma_lock_handler(). We could still get RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED in the small windows between rdma_unlock_handler() and rdma_destroy_id(), but in that case smbdirect_connection_rdma_event_handler() is basically a no-op. 19/11/2026 19/11/2026 Gravedad 3.1 Txt Gravedad 3.1 (CVSS 3.1 Base Score) Pendiente de análisis

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: wait for negotiation before receiving another PDU The receive thread queues a request and can read the next PDU before the negotiation worker finishes. While need_neg is set, the next PDU can cause ksmbd_init_smb_server() to replace conn->ops. A pipelined SMB2 request can therefore make the worker handle an earlier, shorter SMB1 request with SMB2 operations and read beyond its buffer. An SMB1 multi-protocol negotiate may be followed by an SMB2 NEGOTIATE that changes conn->ops again. Wait for work queued while the connection is new or needs negotiation to complete before reading another PDU. This keeps the operations stable for both stages of negotiation without changing when need_neg is cleared. 19/11/2026 19/11/2026 Gravedad 3.1 Txt Gravedad 3.1 (CVSS 3.1 Base Score) Pendiente de análisis

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: serialize directory emptiness checks with readdir SMB2 QUERY_DIRECTORY holds fp->readdir_lock while it calls iterate_dir() on fp->filp. An SMB2 SET_INFO request with FILE_DISPOSITION_INFORMATION can resolve the same FileId and call ksmbd_vfs_empty_dir() on the same filp without that lock. iterate_dir()'s inode read lock permits concurrent readers and does not serialize per-file iterator state. ext4 stores its dx readdir cursor and fname RB tree in file->private_data. Concurrent reset or refill can therefore free a fname node while the other worker still traverses it or retains its RB-tree link, resulting in use-after-free accesses. An authenticated SMB client with list and delete rights on a directory in a writable KSMBD share backed by ext4 can trigger this when the directory takes the dx readdir path. The client overlaps an SMB2 QUERY_DIRECTORY request with an SMB2 SET_INFO request carrying FILE_DISPOSITION_INFORMATION on one live FileId. In one x86_64 SMP KASAN multi-shot guest using ksmbd-for-next at 171df27077fb, the unmodified kernel reported a cross-worker use-after-free before a panic. The first report's access and free stacks show the two request paths directly (trimmed): BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in ext4_htree_store_dirent+0x488/0x550 Read of size 8 by task kworker/2:0/29 Workqueue: ksmbd-io handle_ksmbd_work Call Trace: ext4_htree_store_dirent+0x488/0x550 htree_dirblock_to_tree+0x535/0x990 ext4_htree_fill_tree+0x319/0xba0 ext4_readdir+0x175a/0x2f40 iterate_dir+0x1b6/0x630 smb2_query_dir+0x1003/0x1cc0 Freed by task 279: free_rb_tree_fname+0x67/0xc0 ext4_readdir+0x13a9/0x2f40 iterate_dir+0x1b6/0x630 ksmbd_vfs_empty_dir+0xa2/0x100 smb2_set_info+0x2ffa/0x45d0 Take fp->readdir_lock across the entire emptiness check. This places both iterators over that handle's filp in the same lock domain while preserving the disposition status handling. The exact code change completed a warning-free x86_64 KASAN bzImage build. Tracing three request pairs showed that the two iterate_dir() calls no longer overlapped and the expected statuses were preserved. A further 1,600 reproducer iterations completed with expected statuses and no KASAN report, Oops, or panic. The reproducer and complete guest configuration are available privately to maintainers on request. 19/11/2026 19/11/2026 Gravedad 3.1 Txt Gravedad 3.1 (CVSS 3.1 Base Score) Pendiente de análisis

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ceph: fail readdir when the MDS reply carries no dirfrag A ceph mount oopses in ceph_readdir() when the MDS answers a READDIR request with a reply whose extra blob is empty. parse_reply_info() skips reply blobs whose length is zero, so parse_reply_info_readdir() never runs, r_reply_info.dir_dir stays NULL, and the reply still parses as successful. ceph_mdsc_do_request() returns 0 and ceph_readdir() then reads rinfo->dir_dir->frag with no NULL check: /* extra */ ceph_decode_32_safe(&p, end, len, bad); if (len > 0) { ... err = parse_reply_info_extra(&p, p + len, req, features, s); ... } The oops on v7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820, one getdents64(2) on the mount root after an ms_mode=legacy mount, trimmed: BUG: KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000000-0x0000000000000007] Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc0000000000: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 266 Comm: ls Tainted: G N 7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820 #1 PREEMPT(lazy) RIP: 0010:ceph_readdir+0xbff/0x3ea0 Call Trace: ? __pfx_ceph_readdir+0x10/0x10 wrap_directory_iterator+0xa2/0xe0 iterate_dir+0x1da/0x5d0 __x64_sys_getdents64+0x13b/0x2a0 do_syscall_64+0xdd/0x4a0 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f The unconditional frag read came in with 81c6aea5275ea ("ceph: handle frag mismatch between readdir request and reply"), so the bug is old. Treat a reply with no dirfrag as a protocol violation: warn once, drop the request and return -EIO, the same way ceph_readdir() already handles the two malformed-reply cases later in the function. Tested on v7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820 (KASAN). Unpatched, the getdents64(2) above takes the machine down (oops=panic) on the first READDIR reply. With the patch it warns once and getdents64(2) returns -EIO, no oops, no hang. A conformant reply for an empty directory — dirfrag present, zero entries, FRAG_END|FRAG_COMPLETE — still lists "." and ".." and returns EOF on both kernels, so normal readdir behavior is unchanged. The oops is still present in v7.3-rc5 (72d3fcf802c45). 19/11/2026 19/11/2026 Gravedad 3.1 Txt Gravedad 3.1 (CVSS 3.1 Base Score) Pendiente de análisis

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: blk-crypto: fix NULL deref and UAF in __blk_crypto_evict_key() Sashiko reported a possible NULL pointer dereference, triggered by the following flow: dm-inlinecrypt ctor # first use of the fallback ├─ blk_crypto_init_key() # succeeds, ctx->key.size != 0 ├─ blk_crypto_start_using_key() │ ├─ hw-wrapped key: -EOPNOTSUPP │ │ # profile never allocated (NULL) │ └─ raw key: fallback_start_using_mode() │ └─ blk_crypto_fallback_init() fails │ └─ kfree(profile) # not NULLed ├─ goto bad └─ inlinecrypt_dtr() # evicts whenever key.size is set └─ blk_crypto_evict_key() └─ blk_crypto_config_supported_natively() = false └─ blk_crypto_fallback_evict_key() └─ __blk_crypto_evict_key(blk_crypto_fallback_profile) └─ profile->num_slots # BOOM!!! This issue can be reproduced using the following commands: dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/backing bs=1M count=64 LOOP=$(losetup -f --show /tmp/backing) SZ=$(blockdev --getsz $LOOP) KEY=$(head -c 64 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n') dmsetup create ic --table "0 $SZ inlinecrypt aes-xts-plain64 \ $KEY 0 $LOOP 0 1 keytype:hw-wrapped" And the following oops is triggered: ================================================================== blk-crypto: loop0: no support for wrapped keys Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc000000000b: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN PTI KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000058-0x000000000000005f] CPU: 5 UID: 0 PID: 901 Comm: dmsetup 7.3.0-rc3 #1 PREEMPT(lazy) RIP: 0010:__blk_crypto_evict_key+0x2e/0x3b0 Call Trace: blk_crypto_evict_key+0x24c/0x320 inlinecrypt_dtr+0xf6/0x160 inlinecrypt_ctr+0x2d3/0xbd0 dm_table_add_target+0x661/0xf40 table_load+0x1c4/0x490 ctl_ioctl+0x32f/0x5f0 dm_ctl_ioctl+0xe/0x20 ================================================================== dm-inlinecrypt is the only caller that can evict a key that was never started, as fscrypt frees such a key without evicting it. Fix this by returning early from blk_crypto_fallback_evict_key() when tfms_inited[] is not set for the key's mode. tfms_inited[] is only set after blk_crypto_fallback_init() has successfully initialized the profile, so the crash above is no longer reachable. The bug has been latent since commit c984ff1423ae ("blk-crypto: dynamically allocate fallback profile") was merged in v6.5, and only became actually triggerable when commit e7f57d2c47e2 ("dm-inlinecrypt: add target for inline block device encryption") was merged in v7.2. 19/11/2026 19/11/2026 Gravedad 3.1 Txt Gravedad 3.1 (CVSS 3.1 Base Score) Pendiente de análisis

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ARM: 9524/1: mm: align hugetlb mappings to the huge page size mmap(MAP_HUGETLB) on 32-bit Arm can return an address which is not aligned to the huge page size. In a QEMU virt guest, unmapping the VMA then hits the alignment check in __unmap_hugepage_range(): kernel BUG at mm/hugetlb.c:5213! Internal error: Oops - BUG: 0 [#1] SMP ARM PC is at __unmap_hugepage_range+0x540/0x584 LR is at __zap_vma_range+0x13a0/0x1410 Commit 7bd3f1e1a9ae ("mm: make hugetlb mappings go through mm_get_unmapped_area_vmflags") made hugetlb mappings use the architecture's arch_get_unmapped_area(). The generic implementations handle hugetlb alignment, but the Arm implementations only account for the optional SHMLBA cache-colouring constraint. A 4 KiB-page kernel can therefore align the mapping to 4 KiB or 16 KiB instead of the required 2 MiB. Set the alignment mask from the file's hstate for hugetlb mappings in both Arm implementations. Huge-page alignment also satisfies the SHMLBA constraint. 19/11/2026 19/11/2026 Gravedad 3.1 Txt Gravedad 3.1 (CVSS 3.1 Base Score) Pendiente de análisis

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: wifi: mt76: mt7925: fix reset panic caused by the WM2 rx irq mask mt7925_irq_map sets wm2_complete_mask, but mt7925_dma_layout has no tx done ring, so the MT_RXQ_MCU_WA queue and its NAPI are never set up. On a chip reset, mt7925e_mac_reset() calls napi_disable() on that NAPI and crashes: BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000a40 Workqueue: mt76 mt7925_mac_reset_work [mt7925_common] RIP: 0010:mutex_lock+0x1c/0x50 Call Trace: napi_disable+0x1d/0x50 mt7925e_mac_reset+0x327/0x420 [mt7925e] mt7925_mac_reset_work+0x9a/0x1a0 [mt7925_common] Remove the WM2 mask from mt7925_irq_map and from MT7925_INT_RX_DONE_ALL. 19/11/2026 19/11/2026 Gravedad 3.1 Txt Gravedad 3.1 (CVSS 3.1 Base Score) Pendiente de análisis
